cards.back: About 5,000 account managers, each covering around 20 advertisers. Answers in under 10 seconds; read-only apart from suggestions.
It stays in BigQuery and is queried live. Copying warehouse rows into a vector database gives stale, unfilterable numbers.

cards.front: Why no vector database for the schema
cards.back: 30 to 40 table descriptions are roughly 10K tokens, so they go in a cached system prompt with example questions. Schema retrieval only pays off at hundreds of tables.
pgvector, chunked on headings and paragraphs and tagged with advertiser and access group. Hybrid search, top 20, rerank, keep the best 5.

cards.front: Predefined tools instead of free SQL
cards.back: The model picks a tool and fills parameters; code builds and runs the SQL, so it cannot scan everything or skip a filter. Free SQL is a read-only, dry-run, byte-capped fallback.
Code adds advertiser_id IN (...) from the signed-in session to every query, and BigQuery row-level access policies enforce it again.
Code checks that every number in the answer appears in a tool result. If not, the answer is regenerated or returned as 'I couldn't find that in the data'.
propose_budget_shift creates a card the manager accepts in the normal Ads UI. No tool writes to the account.

cards.front: Rule before showing a budget suggestion
cards.back: Only move budget to B if B loses over 10% of impression share to budget and its cost per conversion is at least 20% better than A's, with 30+ conversions each.
Randomised by advertiser, not by suggestion, for 4 weeks; target conversions or ROAS at equal spend up 3% or more at p < 0.05.
Number accuracy 98% or more, root-cause agreement 80% or more, recall@5 at least 0.9, zero isolation leaks, p95 under 10 s.

quiz.q: A manager asks 'why did CPC go up last week?'. What does the agent check first in the metrics?
choices: Whether cost or clicks moved, and which campaigns explain most of the change
The help docs on CPC
The advertiser's past notes
Free-form SQL over the whole warehouse
quiz.why: CPC is cost divided by clicks, so the agent compares weeks by campaign to see which moved before looking for a cause.

quiz.q: A bug in a tool drops the advertiser filter from one query. What still stops another advertiser's rows coming back?
choices: The model's system prompt
The reranker
BigQuery row-level access policies scoped to the manager
The number check
quiz.why: The warehouse enforces isolation again, so even a buggy query cannot return another advertiser's rows.

quiz.q: The answer says 'spend rose 34%' but no tool result contains 34%. What happens?
choices: It is sent with a warning icon
The check fails and the answer is regenerated or replaced with 'I couldn't find that in the data'
An LLM judge decides whether 34% is plausible
It is sent because the model is usually right
quiz.why: Any number not in a tool result fails the grounded-numbers check.

quiz.q: A teammate wants to embed the 35 table descriptions into a vector store for schema retrieval. What do you say?
choices: Good idea, schema retrieval always helps
Embed sample rows too
Fine-tune the model on the schema instead
At about 10K tokens, put them in a cached system prompt; retrieval only pays off at hundreds of tables
quiz.why: 30 to 40 tables fit in a cached prefix, so a vector database adds parts without benefit.

quiz.q: After launch, 18% of accepted budget suggestions are reverted within 7 days. What does the design say to do?
choices: Nothing; acceptance rate is above 40%
Turn the feature flag off, since reverts above 15% trigger it
Raise the 20% cost-per-conversion bar silently
Switch the A/B test to randomise by suggestion
quiz.why: Reverts above 15% or a ROAS drop turn the feature flag off.

quiz.q: Why is the suggestion A/B test randomised by advertiser rather than by suggestion?
choices: One advertiser's suggestions affect each other, so splitting them contaminates the test
Advertisers are cheaper to count
It makes the test finish in one day
Regulators require it
quiz.why: Budget moves within one advertiser interact, so the unit of randomisation is the advertiser.

quiz.q: p95 latency is 14 s against a 10 s budget. The agent calls metrics, change history, docs and notes one after another. What is the first fix?
choices: Drop the change history call
Use the large model for every step
Run the independent tool calls in parallel
Move campaign data into pgvector
quiz.why: Tool calls with no dependency on each other run in parallel to stay under the latency budget.
